## Expected deliverables

- README.md (modify)

## Out of scope

- Other files

## User defaults that apply

- strangers: Code, commits, docs, and records are written for an outside reader. Here: plain words

## Time budget

Each producer run, the first and any send-back, is stopped after 86400 seconds of wall-clock time. A stopped run sends no report, so what is on disk when it stops must already be a usable change.

Pace the work by its order. Do the smallest change that meets every acceptance criterion first, one file at a time, and leave extras for afterwards; report as soon as the criteria are met. Leave no half-edited file and no broken build between steps. Use targeted tests while you work (`cargo test -p <crate> <filter>`). The full suite runs at most once, and Athena runs it again on your result (see "Checks before the verifier" below), so a second full run only spends this limit.

You have no clock of your own. If the commands Bash may run (below) include `date`, note the time when you start and read it between steps; without it, count steps against the order above.

## Words you must not write

Athena's boundary scan fails any tracked file that names who runs Athena or the machine it runs on. Do not write these words in any file you touch: code, comments, docs, tests, prompts, changelog or design text. The scan matches whole words, case-insensitively, so capital letters do not help; singular, plural and hyphenated forms are all listed. Reword instead.

Words: `operator`, `operators`, `opctl`, `ccr`, `sandbox`, `sandboxes`, `sandboxed`, `lease`, `leases`, `handoff`, `handoffs`, `hand-off`, `hand-offs`, `cloud session`, `cloud sessions`, `remote session`, `remote sessions`

Fragments (rejected anywhere in a line, even inside a longer word or path): `/home/user`, `claude-0/`, `~/.`, `.ccr/`, `claude.ai/code`, `session_01`

Before you finish, run `cargo test -p xtask --test policy` on your changed files. It is the same scan Athena runs, and it names each file, line and word it rejects. Reword any banned word it finds, then run it again until it passes. It reads only tracked files, so it does not see a file you created: reread each new file against the words above.

## Files kept by hand

If `crates/athena-cli/tests/mirrors.rs` exists in your working directory, run `cargo test -p athena-cli --test mirrors` before you finish. A file kept by hand as a mirror of a source (the test timings, the decision log, the CI cache key against the build paths, the ontology) is compared with that source by content, and a failure names the file and the fix. A new test file needs its line in xtask/shard-timings.txt, and docs/decisions.md only gains text after its last line.

## Checks Athena will run

- probe: `true`

You may run them first. Athena runs them again on your result, with the base commit's tool configuration.

## Replay of accepted readings while you work

When your change touches code (a path under `crates/`, or Cargo.toml or Cargo.lock), Athena replays the newest accepted readings through the base build and your candidate build before it judges your report. If your change makes the reading rules refuse more than 10% of them, or more than the share the acceptance criteria declare as "N% of newly refused readings" plus 5 points, your work is sent back with the list of newly refused job ids and the measured share. A rule that is too broad shows up there. Narrow the rule so it refuses what it is meant to refuse; do not hide the cases. A replay that cannot run says `no replay` and never counts as a pass.

## Run the existing tests that read what you change

Before you report, name each output your change alters: status, plan, display or any other printed text. Grep `tests/` and the `#[cfg(test)]` modules for a distinctive line of that output and for the function that prints it. Run each test file found with `cargo test -p <crate> --test <name>` (for example `cargo test -p athena-cli --test mirrors`), or `cargo test -p <crate> <module>` for a unit test. Then run the whole crate with `cargo test -p <crate>`. A section printed unconditionally breaks a test that compares whole output, so look for those first. Cite each command, and the name and assertion of any failing test, in your `criteria_check` evidence.

## Commands Bash may run

(none)

## Working directory

A snapshot of the base commit's files, with a one-commit git repository of its own. records/, the owner's private files, and history are absent by design. Your edits become the candidate.

## Evidence snapshot

Athena copied the real records when this job was dispatched into a read-only directory outside your working copy:

- path: /tmp/.tmpBV7yoN/repo/jobs/20261115-115609-j1g0/evidence

It holds `records/` (every file under records/ at the base commit), `landings/` (the landing records) and `history.json` (the base commit and the newest 200 first-parent commits of main: hash, commit time, subject, trailers). Every check of real records, such as counting jobs, reading an earlier job's records or comparing a claim with history, uses this snapshot and not the working copy. Read it with the Read, Grep and Glob tools, or run `cargo run -p athena-cli -- status --snapshot /tmp/.tmpBV7yoN/repo/jobs/20261115-115609-j1g0/evidence`, which prints the job counts, the history summary and the throughput section from it. It is read-only: a write to it fails. The working copy still has no records/.

## What the verifier sees

The verifier sees only the candidate diff, in a fresh snapshot. It does not see your commands, output, or reasoning. Evidence for a behavior criterion must cite commands the verifier can run itself in that snapshot; your own git status and git diff runs do not count as evidence. Commit hashes made during verification do not exist in the real history, so never pin or cite a commit hash made during verification in code, docs, or design-revision text (BRIEF.md included); describe the content instead. The one exception is the pinned instance: when the brief has a "Pinned source" section, cite its url, ref and SHA as given.

## Make your evidence checkable

Every acceptance criterion must be checkable from the snapshot, the diff or the commands the verifier runs, never from the producer's report or change description, which the verifier does not see. Prefer a test in your change that shows the property. Add a new file for evidence only when a deliverable or a criterion names it. Your report is still where you state what you ran or read; the rule only means the verifier does not rely on it. If a criterion can be shown only from your report, report it unmet and begin its evidence with `not checkable by the verifier`; do not invent a file.

## criteria_check: copy the line

Report exactly one criteria_check entry per acceptance criterion, in the order below, including criteria that were already satisfied before you began. For each entry copy the line below as the entry's criterion text, character for character; do not retype, shorten, merge or reword it. Give its status (met or unmet) and your evidence: what you read or ran. A criterion with no entry is sent back.

A criterion that only Athena's own recorded checks can show (cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy, the full or workspace cargo test) is not yours to run: report it with evidence that starts with "left to Athena's checks" and it is not sent back; the verifier judges it from the recorded checks. Targeted-test criteria and every other criterion must still be reported met with evidence of what you ran or read.

README.md describes the demo

## Planned files left unchanged

Every file in the plan and in the expected deliverables must be changed, or you must say why it needs no change. Before you report, compare your edits with those lists. For each listed file you did not change, either change it now or add an entry to `unchanged_planned_files` in your report with its path and the reason. A listed file that is neither changed nor explained is sent back once, then flagged to the verifier as a gap.

## Checks before the verifier

After you report, Athena usually runs the configured checks (fmt, clippy and the test suite) on your work before the verifier does. A check that fails there, and did not already fail on the base, is sent back to you once, with its command, exit status and output tail, in the same send-back as any unmet criteria. A check still failing after that send-back goes to the verifier as flagged, and the verifier's own run of the checks is the verdict. The run is skipped, with a line saying so, when disk space is low, when no build slot is free, when it hits an error, or when your change holds check-tool configuration, which verification replaces with the base's.

Athena also runs each behavior criterion that names real records and gives a `status --snapshot` command, on your work tree, and records the command and its output for the verifier. It sends you back only when a line that holds the criterion's phrase prints a figure outside the stated range, or a parenthesised list of three or more job ids that all show the same value; other output is only recorded. Do not change what a command prints to satisfy this check.

## If you leave the tree unchanged

A run that leaves the tree unchanged still fails. Set `no_change` in your report, and Athena records it as the job's failure reason: `already_done` with the evidence (the file and symbol you found in place), `blocked` with the blocker, or `gave_up` with the reason. Set it to null when you changed files.

## Report

End with the producer report as your structured output.


## Decisions that govern files you will change

A decision in `docs/decisions.md` governs each path listed below. A change that touches one of them fails before the verifier starts unless the same change reconciles the decision: add an entry (`## D<n> · title`) to `docs/decisions.md` that amends or supersedes the decision, or says it was checked and stands, and add a `[[link]]` to `docs/decision-links.toml` whose `older` is the decision's id and whose `newer` is the new entry's id. Do this in the same change, the first time. A change that still leaves one unreconciled is sent back once with the gate's message, and then fails.

- D02 governs README.md


## Sent back

Your change touches code that a logged decision governs and does not reconcile the decision; the decision gate's message below says how. When no criteria, planned files or replay are listed, that message is the only reason for this send-back, and the rest of this paragraph applies to it as to any other item. Your previous report did not show every acceptance criterion as met in criteria_check, or left planned files unchanged without a reason. Your edits are still in your working directory. Fix the work for each item below, then report every acceptance criterion in criteria_check, copying each line from the brief's criteria_check section as its text, with its status and your evidence. A planned file listed below must be changed, or explained with its path and a reason in unchanged_planned_files in your report. This is the only send-back: if your changes are still in place afterwards, they go to the verifier with the criteria your report still leaves unmet or unreported, and the planned files still unchanged and unexplained, flagged, and the verifier judges them. A run that leaves no change fails.

Decision gate: decisions not reconciled: the change touches code that docs/decisions.md records decisions for: D02 (README.md). Add an entry to docs/decisions.md that amends or supersedes each decision (or says it was checked and stands), and a matching [[link]] in docs/decision-links.toml whose older is the decision and whose newer is the new entry.

summary: The change does what was asked. Links in docs/decision-links.toml are now keyed on their older and newer decision ids, and none carries a `line`. The phrase parser moved into athena_data::decision_links, so the backtest and the new check read the log the same way. A new pure function, `link_problems`, compares the candidate with the base and reports only faults the change introduces: a link that no phrase in the log names, a new phrase that has no link, a new statement that names no id, or a list that does not parse. `decision_gate` runs it when the changed paths include docs/decisions.md, both in the producer loop (`unreconciled_in_snapshot`) and at the candidate gate, so a broken link holds the job before the verifier, with the one send-back. An advisory list of docs lines that cite an amended or superseded id is printed as `decisions  note:` lines and added to a held job's send-back. It never fails a job. D187 is appended after D186 with a Provenance bullet and the phrase `Amends D156`, plus its link. decision-sets.md §8 and CHANGELOG describe the check and the id keying. All 10 changed files are on the deliverables list. I ran `cargo test --locked -p athena-data decision_links` and all 38 tests passed. My targeted athena-core run did not compile: the shared target dir held a stale athena-data library, apparently left there by Athena's revert ("fails without the fix") run. The policy denied `--target-dir`, so I stopped there. For criteria 2, 4, 5 and 7 the evidence is therefore Athena's recorded `cargo test --locked` pass on this commit (CI) plus my reading of the tests (none is `#[ignore]`d), not my own targeted runs. Remaining issues are minor: the advisory list reaches the producer only when the job is held; a job that edits only the toml is not checked; one test is tied to a comment in the toml.
